headline: CORN BACK ABOVE $5 AS RAIN KEEPS COMBINES PARKED
lead: Corn closed $5.00, up 4 and a quarter cents, clawing back the round number it lost Friday while El Nino rain keeps the Belt's combines sitting in the shed. Soybean oil ran 2.7% on the back of soymeal's firm tone, the two products pulling in the same direction for once.
teaser: Corn reclaims $5.00 as historic rain keeps the Belt's combines parked and harvest basis frozen.

one_number.unit: cent weekly decline range cited Friday, now reversing
one_number.context: AgWeb flagged corn and beans down 20 to 40 cents on the week Friday; Monday's bounce claws back roughly a dime of that on harvest-delay buying alone.

sections.title: Corn Reclaims The Round Number
sections.body:
- Corn closed **$5.00**, up 4 and a quarter cents, one session after AgWeb's Friday headline had the whole complex down 20 to 40 cents for the week.
- AgWeb's record El Nino rain story is the driver: combines parked, farmers can't deliver, and that's bullish basis even while board direction stays shaky.
sections.so_what: Rain is doing what demand news hasn't: putting a floor under the board.

sections.title: Soy Complex Leads On Products
sections.body:
- Soybean oil gained 2.7% to $68.27, the day's biggest mover and flagged overnight, with soymeal firm too at $344.30, up 0.8%.
- Beans themselves lagged the products, up just six and three-quarters cents to $12.89, so this is a crush story, not a bean-demand story.
sections.so_what: Products leading beans says crush margins, not export demand, are driving today.

sections.title: Cattle Soft, Feeders Give More Back
sections.body:
- Live cattle eased 0.2% to $218.85 and feeders dropped 1.4% to $334.62, continuing the pullback from the historic summer run.
- The screwworm border story is still the backdrop. Mexican feeder imports stay closed until the Aug 24 phased reopening at Douglas, now well behind us, so today's softness isn't a supply-return story.
sections.so_what: Feeders are fading faster than fed cattle, a spread worth tracking into winter placements.

outside_the_pit.title: Farm Bureau Presses Trump On Diesel Relief
outside_the_pit.body: Zippy Duvall asked Trump to suspend the federal highway diesel tax as fuel costs squeeze harvest-season operating margins right when combines need the fuel most.

watch_list.desc: Harvest pace reports; continued rain delays keep basis firm even if board direction stays mixed.
Corn above $5.00 is the line; a close back below reopens Friday's selloff.
Export sales; soybeans under 300K MT would undercut today's product-led strength.
